note: For F(a,b,c)=a^3+b^3+c^3-3abc, use F=(a+b+c)Q, Q=a^2+b^2+c^2-ab-bc-ca. If 3|F then F mod 3 equals a+b+c mod 3, hence 3 divides the sum; substituting c congruent to -a-b mod 3 gives Q congruent to 3(a^2+ab+b^2)=0 mod 3, so 9|F. Sufficiency: N=3r+1 use (a,b,c)=(r+1,r,r); N=3r+2 use (r,r+1,r+1); N=9t, t>=1 use (t+1,t,t-1); N=0 use (0,0,0). Each triple is nonnegative and direct expansion/factorization gives N.
